newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee quarter, year aided by each of its divisions.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee quarter, year aided by each of its divisions.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp. Thursday reported higher earnings for its fourth quarter and full fiscal year, as each of its four lines of business improved.

Sara Lee, a global food and consumer products company, said it earned $280 million, or 57 cents a primary share, in the fourth quarter, up from $259 million, or 52 cents per share. Sales rose to $4.9 billion from $4.6 billion.
For the year, earnings rose to $1.0 billion, or $2.03 a share, from $916.0 million, or $1.83 a share, the previous year. Sales grew to $19.7 billion from $18.6 billion.

Sara Lee, based in Chicago, markets a wide variety of products including Sara Lee, Ball Park, Hillshire Farm, Jimmy Dean, Aoste, Douwe Egberts, Hanes, Hanes Her Way, L'eggs, Bali, Playtex, Champion, Coach, Dim, Sanex and Kiwi.

Packaged Meats and Bakery sales rose 15.4 percent to $1.9 billion in the fourth quarter, while operating income gained 10.5 percent to $134 million. For the year, its sales gained 16.6 percent to $7.6 billion and earnings rose 12.8 percent to $476 million.
Profit growth was particularly strong in packaged meats and foodservice during both periods, with double-digit gains, excluding acquisitions, Sara Lee said.
Bakery sales and profits fell in the quarter and year, reflecting a weak U.S. retail market for frozen baked goods.

Coffee and grocery sales for the fourth quarter rose 4.1 percent to $724 million, while operating income rose 2.5 percent to $100 million. For the year sales fell 2.9 percent to $2.8 billion, while operating income rose 2.9 percent to $440 million.
Results reflect the negative impact of a stronger dollar, Sara Lee said. In local currencies, sales increased during both periods and profits were up more than 10 percent.

Household and Body Care fourth quarter sales rose 2 percent to $524 million and operating income gained 6.3 percent to $85 million. For the fiscal year, sales were up 0.3 percent to $1.8 billion and profits gained 6.4 percent to $228 million.

Personal products sales rose 0.7 percent in the fourth quarter to $1.8 billion and operating income rose 6.3 percent to $215 million. For the year, sales increased 1.5 percent to $7.5 billion and profits gained 4.4 percent to $761 million.
Sara Lee stock was down 87.5 cents at $43.75 at mid-afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange.
